messages:
rachel: quick heads-up, saw a p99 regression in chatstream after the recent kernel swap (attn-fused -> flash-attn-v2). raw dashboards show streaming tail widening while non-streaming completions actually got slightly faster. :thinking:
leo: can you paste the perf snippet? which workload / mb sizes?
jamie: fwiw our rolling canary used mbsize=4 for both streaming and completions — might be the wrong parity to test streaming behavior.
rachel: here's the trimmed profile from last night (10k reqs sample) -- streaming = SSE stream enabled; completions = sync response path:

```
# streaming, mb=1,2,4,8 (p50/p95/p99 ms)
mb=1: 30 / 120 / 320
mb=2: 28 / 95 / 220
mb=4: 26 / 80 / 410  # weird jump at p99
mb=8: 40 / 150 / 600
\n# completions, mb=1,2,4,8 (p50/p95/p99 ms)
mb=1: 35 / 110 / 180
mb=2: 33 / 90 / 200
mb=4: 31 / 85 / 210
mb=8: 45 / 140 / 390
```

maria: interesting — streaming p99 at mb=4 spikes a lot compared to mb=2. suggests tail interactions with KV cache or kernel fallback under higher batch sizes.
leo: do we have kernel-level traces? any kernel switch logs around those p99s?
perf-bot: trace snapshot attached (trace id: trace-2026-03-12-ff12). top reasons: kernel_requeue (37%), kv_miss_eviction (22%), handshake_wait (18%).
jamie: KV miss + eviction at tail aligns with larger mb causing more hot-key churn across concurrent requests. streaming also keeps KV cache hot per-client; microbatching too big may evict other in-flight clients.
rachel: hypothesis: for streaming we should bias towards smaller mb (1-2) and prefer attn kernel A for low-latency handshake path, while completions can tolerate bigger mb (4-8) and use flash-attn-v2 for throughput.
leo: agreed. quick experiment plan:
- split routing: streaming -> pool-stream (mb_policy=max(2)), completions -> pool-bulk (mb_policy=max(8))
- kernel hint: pool-stream prefers attn-lowlat (fallback flash-attn-v2), pool-bulk prefers flash-attn-v2
- enable kv-prefetch for pool-stream with warmup window=4s

can we run a short A/B canary tomorrow?
maria: +1. i'll create a canary with 10k streaming requests and 10k completion requests, same prompt distribution. logs to perf-traces, p95/p99 delta tracked.
jamie: also add a microprofiler hook to record per-kernel durations and kv cache hit-rate per-client id. put sample command in the canary job:

```
redwood-perf run --canary-id=mbstream-20260313 \
  --routes streaming:pool-stream,completions:pool-bulk \
  --samples 10000 --profile kernel,kv,handshake
```

leo: if the canary verifies, we should make the pool routing change and add MB heuristics: prefer mb=1 for <=50ms client SLAs, mb=2 for <=200ms, else bulk. also add a safeguard to lower mb when kv_miss_rate > 10%.
rachel: noted. i've opened INF-5234 to track this and assigned to @leo. will include links to traces and the perf-bot snapshot. description: "Tune mb sizing + kernel hints to reduce streaming p99 tail while preserving completions throughput."
perf-bot: created INF-5234 (owner: leo) — checklist items: canary, kernel-hint rollout, kv-prefetch tuning, rollback plan.
leo: i'll kick off the canary at 09:00 PT. heads-up if anyone sees unusual error spikes. :eyes:
jamie: one more ask — let's capture per-route token distribution; if streaming prompts skew longer, that could amplify tail. add that to the profiler.
maria: done. canary job includes prompt_len histogram.
rachel: thanks all. if canary looks good, plan to rollback kernel swap for streaming pools only (keep flash-attn-v2 for bulk) and ship mb heuristics next week.
leo: sounds good. will post results here after the run. :thumbsup:
